title: rivet-voice-19 focus items — operator entity-resolution closed loop
description: One case per rivet-voice-19 focus item that is operator-reachable today (B7.4 add_note, B5.3 reassign_appointment, B6.3 log_time_entry, B4.7 create_appointment / reschedule_appointment / cancel_appointment), plus a negative case pinning the B5.3 resolver fix. Unlike test/voice/fixtures/operator-ops-top-40.json, cases here carry NO pre-resolved ids: every id in `expect` is a `seedRef` resolved by the runner against a REAL Postgres-seeded tenant via the REAL PgEntityResolver, so the corpus proves the spoken free-text reference produces the resolved id end to end, not just that a task handler accepts an id it was handed. `payloadContainsSeedRefs` maps a payload key to a key in the runner's `seedIds` map; `payloadContains` carries literal (non-id) values. `taskResponse` is the SECOND scripted gateway reply, present only for the one intent whose task handler makes its own drafting round-trip (create_appointment); every other handler here is a documented passthrough.

cases.utterance: Note on the Patel job — wants morning visits
Assign Carlos to the Johnson job
Clock 2 hours on the Patel job
Book Garcia for a water heater repair Thursday at 10 AM
cases.note: The CREATE leg of B4.7's conjunctive requirement (book/move/cancel by speaking). The other two legs resolve an EXISTING appointment; this one resolves the customer the booking is for. The scripted drafting reply deliberately carries a HALLUCINATED customerId that matches nothing in the tenant — the drafted payload must still carry the PgEntityResolver's id for the spoken name 'Garcia', because CreateAppointmentAITaskHandler overwrites the model's customerId with the resolved one (create-appointment-task.ts, 'the LLM is instructed never to invent a customerId'). No id in this case's script is ever echoed into an assertion, so nothing here can pass by hand-feeding. scheduledStart/End are produced by the REAL resolveDateTime from the verbatim spoken phrase against the tenant's timezone at the fixed NOW (Mon 2026-08-03 12:00 Chicago) — stored UTC, rendered in tenant tz by the companion it-block.

cases.utterance: Move the Garcia job to Thursday at 10
Assign Carlos to the Fitzgerald job
cases.note: 'Fitzgerald' names no customer/job this tenant has. Pre-fix, PgEntityResolver.resolveAppointment fell straight through to the tenant-wide soonest-upcoming-appointment fallback for ANY non-date, non-job-anchored reference, so this would have silently resolved to Johnson's or Garcia's appointment. Post-fix (b5.3-design.md §3), a name-bearing reference that matches no job returns not_found and is never allowed to reach that fallback — the proposal must gate on appointmentId instead of picking an arbitrary appointment. The technician side (Carlos) resolves fine on its own, isolating the assertion to appointment resolution specifically.
